symptom: The first synthetic total-order matrix CI failed one new antisymmetry assertion on an equal-rank pair: actual 0, expected -0. The comparator itself returned equality correctly. The verify Test step exited 1, while research-governance and post-job cleanup succeeded; no runner/platform failure or production behavior change was evidenced.
lesson: Negating Math.sign(0) produces negative zero, which node:assert/strict distinguishes from positive zero. A red synthetic comparator test can therefore be a fixture expectation error rather than a chronology or runtime comparator defect.
guardrail: For bidirectional ordering assertions derive the reverse expected sign directly from reversed ranks (Math.sign(right.rank - left.rank)), not unary negation of a possibly zero expected sign. Confirm the exact failing assertion in the complete verify log, distinguish it from production/research payload behavior, and verify the corrected source on a new pinned CI head.
